papers.title: Constant query LCCs over the reals
papers.abstract: This note describes a new construction, found by ChatGPT Astra, of constant query Locally Correctable Codes (LCCs) over the real numbers. Prior constructions of constant query LCCs were exclusive to fields of positive characteristic and were conjectured not to exist over the reals. The construction uses low degree polynomial evaluations over an integer grid, together with a novel sampling procedure which outputs, for a given grid point $P$, a random quadratic curve through $P$ which intersects the grid in many other points (the decoding queries). The sampler is `smooth' in the sense that no grid point is queried with high probability. These codes have the additional property that the queried locations (the curve/grid intersections) are all nearby grid points.

papers.title: Feedback Vertex Set, Max Cut, and Edge Coloring on the Strong Product of a Graph and a Path
papers.abstract: We examine the computational complexity of well-known problems on subgraphs of the strong product of two paths. Namely, for Max Cut we show NP-hardness on induced subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$ answering a question by Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Huynh, Joret, Liu, and Wood (2021). For 3-Edge Coloring we show NP-hardness on subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$ and that it is equivalent to 3-Edge Coloring on planar graphs for induced subgraphs of $P \boxtimes P$. It is a long standing open question whether 3-Edge Coloring on planar graphs is NP-hard. As a second contribution, we consider graphs of the form $G \boxtimes P$ and show that Feedback Vertex Set on these graphs is FPT in the clique-width of $G$. Furthermore, we show that it can be solved in polynomial time if $G$ is chordal or co-comparable and that the computational complexity depends on the parity of $P$ if $G$ is bipartite. Namely, it is solvable in polynomial time if $P$ has an even number of vertices but is NP-complete otherwise. For Max Cut, we show that it can be solved in polynomial time if $G$ is bipartite.

papers.title: The Monophonic Directed Convexities
papers.abstract: Graph Convexity is a topic with many papers in the literature, especially on the $P_3$, geodesic, and monophonic convexities in undirected graphs. Regarding directed graphs, Erd{\H o}s et al. in 1972 and Chartrand and Zhang in 2000 obtained the first results on the $P_3$ and geodesic convexities for directed graphs, respectively. In this paper, we start the investigation of monophonic convexity on directed graphs. We define two convexities, the monophonic and the strong monophonic directed convexities, related to the minimal and the induced directed paths, respectively. We show that deciding whether a set is convex is polynomial-time solvable in the monophonic convexity, but coNP-complete in the strong monophonic convexity. For both convexities, we prove that the hull number is NP-complete even in DAGs. Regarding the monophonic convexity, we prove that the hull number is polynomial time solvable in tournaments, but the interval number is NP-complete in tournaments and also in bipartite oriented graphs.

papers.title: Unilluminable rooms: minimal examples, classifications and exceptions
papers.abstract: A room with mirrored walls can contain two points that are mutually invisible: no light ray from one reaches the other. Tokarsky built the first polygonal examples by tiling a room with reflected copies of a triangle and making every tile vertex of certain kinds a corner of the room. We study the smallest rooms of this kind, which we call lattice rooms. Their interior tile vertices of the remaining kind, the sources, are invisible and pairwise mutually invisible. On the tiling by isosceles right triangles, a hole-free lattice room with a source has at least 12 sides, attained only by the pinwheel. On the square tiling the least number is 16, again attained by one room. A hole-free lattice room with two sources has at least 24 sides on the first tiling and 34 on the square tiling. Up to congruence there are 12 such rooms with 24 sides, 89 with 25 sides and 14 with 34 sides. One absorbing post, one partition, or one hole that touches the outer boundary at one point lowers the least number of sides for two sources to 18, 20 and 22 (21 if sides are counted as maximal straight segments). Two and three posts give 17 and 16 sides, and a hole that does not touch the outer boundary gives 26. We list all smallest rooms. Rooms assembled from n modules have exactly 12n sides and n sources, and a hole-free lattice room with three or more sources has at least 36 sides. We also give rooms in which some tile vertices need not be corners: 15 types of 27-sided rooms on the tiling by triangles with angles 30, 60 and 90 degrees, which are smallest in their class, a nonagon with three mutually invisible corners, and a 42-sided room in which a rotation through 180 degrees takes the place of a corner. In a ring of three trapezoids a light ray returns to a corner that is invisible in one trapezoid. Several classifications rely on exhaustive computer searches made finite by the bounds proved here.

papers.title: Linear-size graphs at every strict dismantling level
papers.abstract: Dismantling reduces a graph to one vertex by successive deletions. At level zero, a vertex is eligible if one of its neighbours is adjacent to all its other neighbours. At level $k\geq1$, its neighbours must induce a graph dismantlable at level $k-1$. A graph has strict level $k$ if it admits a reduction at level $k$ and none at level $k-1$. For every $k\geq1$, we construct a graph of strict level $k$ with $3k+8$ vertices. Each step adds three vertices: the neighbours of one induce the preceding graph, and the other two provide the adjacencies used to rule out other first deletions at the lower level. A second construction gives a graph of order $4k+4$ at strict level $k$. Together the two families give the upper bound $\min\{4k+4,3k+8\}$ on the least order at strict level $k$.

papers.title: Combinatorial optimization with bounded subdeterminants
papers.abstract: We take a first step toward a broader study of classical combinatorial optimization problems through the maximum subdeterminants of their standard integer programming formulations, yielding new positive results for several famous (NP-hard) problems. An integer matrix is totally $\Delta$-modular if every square submatrix has determinant of absolute value at most $\Delta$. For every fixed $\Delta$, it has been known that maximum clique, maximum stable set, and minimum vertex cover can be solved in polynomial time on instances for which the coefficient matrix of the natural formulation is totally $\Delta$-modular. We extend this list by showing that the same holds for many other problems, including the weighted versions of maximum cut, the traveling salesman problem, feedback vertex set, odd cycle transversal, dominating set, max 2-sat, induced matching, and cluster vertex deletion, as well as for $k$-colorability and graph isomorphism. Our proofs reveal several new ways in which bounded subdeterminants impose combinatorial structure: they bound the size or maximum degree of the input graph, bound packings of cycles and other obstructions, or yield decompositions into tractable graph classes such as forests, chordal graphs, graphs of bounded treewidth, and graphs of bounded linear mim-width.

papers.title: Approximating graphic TSP by b-matchings
papers.abstract: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for graphic TSP that returns a tour of length at most $\frac{89}{64}=\frac{7}{5}-\frac{3}{320}$ times the value of the subtour relaxation. This improves the long-standing ratio $\frac75$ of Seb\H{o} and Vygen and shows that the integrality gap of the subtour LP on graphic instances is at most $\frac{89}{64}\approx 1.3906$. We optimize a non-linear objective function over an odd-join polytope, which uses (i) a new removable system of edges, and (ii) reconnection of subtours if the graph is disconnected. This approach gives a $\frac{13}{10}$-approximation algorithm for $4$-regular $4$-vertex-connected graphs, improving the $\frac43$ of Newman, and a $\frac43$-approximation for $k$-vertex-connected graphs of maximum degree at most $k+1$, for every $k\ge 3$. For the general graphic TSP, we construct a feasible point in the odd-join polytope, using an optimal vertex from the Subtour linear programming relaxation of TSP, which helps us bound the approximation factor by 89/64.

papers.title: A note on the intractability of enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression
papers.abstract: We show that, given a Horn expression and a family of inclusion-wise maximal satisfiable subsets of its clauses, deciding whether there exists another maximal satisfiable subset is NP-complete. As a consequence, unless P=NP, there is no output-polynomial time algorithm enumerating the maximal satisfiable subformulas of a Horn expression.

papers.title: Online Graph Coloring: Competitive Ratios Separating Randomized and Deterministic Algorithms
papers.abstract: We study online coloring, focusing on the competitive ratio. The best previously known results were (1) a lower bound of $\Omega(n / \log^2 n)$ for both deterministic and randomized algorithms by Halld\'{o}rsson and Szegedy (1994), (2) an upper bound of $O(n / \log n)$ for randomized algorithms by Halld\'{o}rsson (1997), and (3) an upper bound of $O(n / \log \log n)$ for deterministic algorithms by Kawarabayashi, Yoneda, and Yoneda (2025). In this paper, we improve these results as follows: 1. A new lower bound of $\Omega(n / \log n)$ for deterministic algorithms. 2. A new upper bound of $O(n (\log \log n)^2 / \log^2 n)$ for randomized algorithms. 3. A new upper bound of $O(n / (\log \log n)^{2-\varepsilon})$ for deterministic algorithms for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. For randomized algorithms, we nearly close the gap between the lower and upper bounds; the remaining gap is only $O((\log \log n)^2)$. We establish the asymptotic separation between randomized and deterministic online graph coloring. Against an oblivious adversary, a polynomial-time randomized algorithm achieves a competitive ratio asymptotically smaller than any deterministic algorithm can guarantee, even with unlimited computation.

papers.title: Rotating Walks, Derandomized Squares, and Permutation Conjugated Walks
papers.abstract: Using the recent strong convergence results of Bordenave and Collins (Annals of Mathematics) and Chen et al. (Annals of Mathematics), we study the average case behavior of rotating random walks of Cohen and Maor (STOC 2023) and the derandomized square construction of Rozenman and Vadhan (RANDOM 2005). Concretely, we prove a conjecture of Cohen et al. (ITCS 2025) regarding the average case behavior of derandomized squaring for random graphs and show that the existential bounds of Cohen and Maor for their rotating random walk construction hold with high-probability for random graphs. Using the results of O'Donnell and Wu (FOCS 2020), we can in polynomial time construct a family of graphs and rotations which almost saturate the bounds of Cohen and Maor, and meet the bounds conjectured by Cohen et al. for all vertex-transitive auxiliary graphs of fixed degree in the derandomized square. Finally, we study independent random permutation conjugates of deterministic regular graph adjacency matrices. We prove quantitative weak convergence to freely independent tree adjacency operators when the degrees are fixed and the girths tend to infinity. Separately, a covering argument gives deterministic spectral lower bounds for polynomials with non-negative coefficients, recovering the lower bound of Cohen et al. for rotating walks.

papers.title: Optimal radio labelings for the Cartesian product of a path and the Heawood graph
papers.abstract: For a simple graph $G$, let $d(u,v)$ denote the distance between two vertices $u$ and $v$ in $G$, and let $diam(G)$ denote the diameter of $G$. A radio labeling of $G$ is a mapping $f : V(G) \rightarrow \mathbb{N} \cup \{0\}$ such that $|f(u)-f(v)|\geq diam(G) + 1 - d(u,v)$ holds for every pair of distinct vertices $u, v \in G$. The span of $f$ is the difference between the largest and smallest integers assigned by $f$, and the radio number $rn(G)$ is the minimum span taking over all radio labelings of $G$. Let $P_n$ denote the path on $n$ vertices and let $H$ denote the Heawood graph (see Figure-1). In this paper we determine the radio number for the Cartesian product of a path and the Heawood graph, and characterize all optimal radio labelings of $P_n \Box H$. Moreover, we show that the radio number of $P_n \Box H$ exceed the lower bound given for $rn(G)$ in [6], where $G$ is any graph, and that this gap is arbitrarily large.

papers.title: You Can Have It All: Small sparse induced-universal graphs for minor-closed classes
papers.abstract: We show that, for every fixed proper minor-closed graph class $\mathcal{G}$ and every positive integer $n$, there exists a graph $U_n$ with $n^{1+o(1)}$ vertices and edges such that every $n$-vertex graph in $\mathcal{G}$ is isomorphic to an induced subgraph of $U_n$. This result generalizes and unifies the results of Dujmovi\'c et al. (J. ACM 2021) on induced-universal graphs and the results of Esperet, Joret, and Morin (J. London Math. Soc. 2023) on sparse induced-universal graphs from planar graphs to all proper minor-closed graph classes. It simultaneously improves the previous bounds for the number of vertices in induced-universal graphs (previously $O(n^2)$ obtained as a corollary of a result of DeVos et al. (J. Comb. Theory, Ser. {B} 2004) and a result of Gavoille and Labourel (ESA 2007)) and the number of edges in subgraph-universal graphs (previously $O(n^{3/2})$ by Babai et al. (Theory and Practice of Combinatorics 1982)).

papers.title: Bounding and Approximating Kostka Numbers
papers.abstract: Kostka numbers, the coefficients of Schur polynomials, count semistandard Young tableaux of prescribed shape and weight. We give a deterministic algorithm for approximating Kostka numbers within a simply exponential factor in the number of variables and the size of the partition. Our approach combines Gurvits capacity bounds for log-concave polynomials with an algorithm for approximating the Gurvits capacity of a Schur polynomial. For a Schur polynomial in $n$ variables indexed by $\lambda$, we show that the logarithm of the capacity associated with any nonzero coefficient can be approximated to additive error $\epsilon$ in time polynomial in $n$, $|\lambda|$, and $\log(1/\epsilon)$. The analysis establishes an explicit bounded optimization region and efficient approximate first-order oracles, and handles boundary weights through a factorization into smaller Schur polynomials.

papers.title: Characterizing Fixed-Treewidth Planar Graphs
papers.abstract: We give the first inductive characterization of planar graphs of treewidth $k$ for each $k \geq 3$. Our definition generalizes the well-known inductive definition of planar $3$-trees and the recent definition of so-called planar quasi-$4$-trees [F\"orster, 2024]. As a key step, which may be of independent interest, we show that every planar triangulation $G$ of treewidth $k$ admits a tree decomposition of width $k$ where each adhesion set induces a cycle in $G$. As an application of planar quasi-$4$-trees, we show that planar graphs of treewidth at most $4$ have vertex arboricity at most $2$. That is, the vertex-set of every planar graph of treewidth at most $4$ can be partitioned into two sets that each induce a forest.

papers.title: Maximum Probability of Independence in Transitive Matroids
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a matroid on a finite ground set $E$, and suppose that the automorphism group of $M$ acts transitively on $E$. We show the following: if $X_1,\ldots,X_K$ are sampled independently from a distribution $p$ on $E$, then the probability that the samples are distinct and that $\{X_1,\ldots,X_K\}$ is an independent set in $M$ is quasi-concave in $p$ and maximized when $p$ is uniform. For $2\le K\le\rank(M)$, we characterize all maximizers by uniform total mass on the parallel classes and, in particular, show that the maximizer is unique and has global quadratic stability when $M$ is simple. As a corollary, for a random $K\times N$ matrix over a finite field with i.i.d.\ rows, uniform sampling from the nonzero vectors maximizes the probability of full row rank. Finally, we show that uniform sampling maximizes $\Prob\big(\rank_M(X_1,\ldots,X_L)\ge r\big)$, and hence also $\E\rank_M(X_1,\ldots,X_L)$, for every $L, r$.

papers.title: List coloring uncrowded hypergraphs at the shattering threshold
papers.abstract: A foundational theorem of Ajtai, Koml\'os, Pintz, Spencer, and Szemer\'edi asserts that every $n$-vertex $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph (i.e., with girth at least $5$) of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ contains an independent set of size $cn(\log\Delta/\Delta)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. Improving an earlier bound of Frieze and Mubayi, Iliopoulos showed that every such hypergraph has list chromatic number at most $(1+o(1))(k-1)(\Delta/\log\Delta)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$. Determining the optimal leading constant in this bound remains a major open problem. A natural target, suggested by the coupon-collector heuristic, is $(k-1)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, which also corresponds to the shattering threshold for coloring sparse random hypergraphs. Our main result shows that this target is attained: for every integer $k\ge2$, every $k$-uniform uncrowded hypergraph of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ satisfies: $$\chi_\ell(\mathcal{H})\le(1+o(1))\Big((k-1)\frac{\Delta}{\log\Delta}\Big)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}.$$ In particular, this confirms a 2019 conjecture of Molloy for uncrowded hypergraphs. Building on this result, we prove that every $k$-uniform linear hypergraph of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ has chromatic number at most $(c_k+o(1))(\Delta/\log\Delta)^{\frac{1}{k-1}}$, where $c_k\to1$ as $k\to\infty$, thereby proving a conjecture of Verstra\"ete and Wilson on the independence number of linear hypergraphs in the stronger form of colorings. Our techniques also yield a palette sparsification theorem for uncrowded hypergraphs, partially answering a question of Casselgren and Eriksson.

papers.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
papers.abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $\gamma_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_j\gamma_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14,639,440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.

papers.title: Geometry-Dependent Dimension Jumps in Planar $C^r$ Splines at Degree $2r+1$
papers.abstract: We study geometric dependence of the dimensions of planar spline spaces $S_{2r+1}^r$ through families with a single moving interior vertex and determine their dimensions throughout the admissible parameter domains. For $r=1$, we extend the Wu--Deng one-parameter classification to the interior of the central quadrilateral. The dimension increases by one at exactly two isolated points, one due to a local direction-count change and the other to a global compatibility defect. For $r=2$, subdividing one triangle of the Yuan--Stillman configuration gives a twelve-triangle family with fixed local direction counts; its dimension increases by one precisely on an open line segment. For every $r\ge3$, we construct a family with $2r+12$ triangles and fixed local direction counts, proving geometric dependence at degree $2r+1$. The moving vertex lies in an open triangle, and the dimension exceeds Schumaker's lower bound by one exactly on its symmetry axis. The lower collinear vertices may have arbitrary strictly ordered heights. The low-order proofs use exact cofactor elimination. For higher orders, weighted interpolation and block elimination bound the global defect by one, and explicit extension and obstruction arguments determine the exceptional set.

papers.title: Cyclically covering subspaces and additive perfect codes
papers.abstract: Let $h_q(n)$ be the largest codimension of a subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ whose cyclic shifts cover the whole space. For $r>0$, we characterize the inequality $h_q(n)\ge r$ in terms of cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear codes over vector alphabets with covering radius one, no nonzero word of block weight one, and a scalar dual generated by the shifts of one word. For $k,m\ge2$, let $I_q(j)$ count the monic irreducible polynomials of degree $j$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$. If $k$ is prime or $m\ge2\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}I_q(j)+2$, we prove that a cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$ linear perfect code of length $\frac{q^{km}-1}{q^k-1}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q^k$ exists if and only if $\gcd(m,q-1)=1$. When this condition holds, we also obtain \(h_q\!\left(\frac{q^{km}-1}{q^k-1}\right)=k(m-1).\) Restriction of scalars gives the same criterion for every $m\ge2$ when $q$ is odd, $q+1$ is a power of two, and $k=2p$ with $p$ prime. We also show that $h_q(q^k+1)=k$ exactly when $q$ is even, for every $k\ge1$.

papers.title: Explicit restricted isometries with $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit family of real $m\times n$ restricted isometries with $m\to\infty$, $m/n\to 0$, $\delta_k\to 0$, and $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$. We combine Gershgorin's circle theorem with a flat RIP estimate to reduce the problem to choosing a large vertex set in a strongly regular graph with the property that every small subset spans few edges. We select this vertex set using an incidence geometric result due to Zahl. The proof only uses the entrywise absolute value of the Gram matrix despite the conventional wisdom that such proof techniques exhibit a barrier of $m^{1/2}$. We prove that this barrier is actually $m^{2/3}$, and we show that our particular construction exhibits the same barrier.

papers.title: Affine Springer fibers, Cherednik algebra modules and Hilbert schemes: torus link case
papers.abstract: For a pair of positive integers $M,N$ with GCD $d$, we relate the bigraded $S_N\times S_d$-Frobenius characters of the homology of the positive part of a homogeneous affine Springer fiber for $\mathrm{GL}_N$ of slope $M/N$ to a direct sum of the associated graded of minimal supported modules of type $A_{N-1}$ rational Cherednik algebra at the same slope, and to the equivariant K-theory of a coherent sheaf on the Hilbert scheme of points on the plane. For the first object, we use the Hessenberg paving of Goresky-Kottwitz-Macpherson; for the second and third objects, we resort to an explicit Hodge module on $\mathfrak{sl}_N$. The bridge between them is a non-coprime shuffle theorem of Kim-Oh.

papers.title: Multivariate diagonal harmonics: character polynomials and proofs of two conjectures of Bergeron
papers.abstract: We prove Bergeron's Hook-Components and Coefficient-Length conjectures for the Vandermonde polarization module and full diagonal harmonics in every rank and number of alphabets. Hook-label characters are elementary skewings of the alternating character, and the maximal Schur length in label $\mu$ is $n-\mu_1$. We compute character and dimension polynomials of diagonal coinvariants in every bosonic--fermionic superspace for $D\ge3$, $n\ge\max\{D,2D-6\}$, answering Church--Ellenberg--Farb's character and dimension questions. For augmented commutative algebras in characteristic zero, we construct natural two-Schur presentations and filtered free resolutions with one Schur generator in each homological degree. For polynomial algebras, specialization to orthogonal idempotents identifies the first unstable correction for every nonempty tail $\tau$ and degree $D>|\tau|$. The stable threshold $n\ge D+\tau_1$ is sharp when the row dimension is at least $\ell(\tau)$. First parabolic algebras recover finite jets, their multiplication and their maps. Selected-label lifts give uniform Vandermonde generation through degree $D$ for $D\ge3$, $n\ge2D-3$, and disjoint-label products generate every first occurrence for positive integral row weights. Constructive degree reflection determines all two-column moment homology and generates its first syzygies from degree $n+1$; two-column Vandermonde generation reduces to degree $n-1$. Invariants and harmonics separate through the character range and through degree $n$ in two alphabets. The hook identities also give the fully graded sign component of the $t=0$, $(1,2)$-superspace Theta conjecture.

papers.title: Koszul duality and determinant formulas for affine hyperplane arrangements
papers.abstract: For real affine hyperplane arrangements, we prove Lam's determinant conjecture for the inverse Varchenko matrix restricted to bounded chambers. The proof combines Lam's comparison of twisted intersection forms with the period determinant formula of Varchenko, Loeser-Sabbah and Douai-Terao. For normal crossing arrangements, we introduce the taut path algebra and the chamber intersection algebra and establish a Koszul duality between them, yielding an explicit multivariate formula for the inverse Varchenko matrix. After specializing the parameters to $q$, its restriction to bounded chambers is a scalar multiple of the $q$-intersection matrix, proving a determinant conjecture of the authors. We also discuss how the Koszul duality results generalize to affine oriented matroids.

papers.title: Cluster-theoretic Newton--Okounkov polytopes of flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$
papers.abstract: Newton--Okounkov bodies have been used for studying toric degenerations of flag varieties. We classify the Newton--Okounkov polytopes associated with cluster valuations and the anticanonical line bundle on full flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$. In type $A_4$, the $672$ seeds of cluster type $D_6$ yield $162$ affine unimodular equivalence classes, which coincide with the combinatorial equivalence classes. We determine the subgroup of exchange-graph automorphisms preserving every polytope class. It is a Klein four group of index six in the automorphism group of the exchange graph of cluster type $D_6$. In type $B_2$, we give defining inequalities for all six seeds. At the anticanonical weight, the two combinatorial equivalence classes split into three affine unimodular equivalence classes. Their respective class-preserving automorphism groups have orders four and two.

papers.title: The elliptic Hall algebra and the combinatorics of affine Springer fibers
papers.abstract: For coprime positive integers $m,n$ and $k\ge1$, we study the symmetric functions $e_k[-X^{m,n}Y]\cdot1$ arising from the elliptic Hall algebra action. We identify their $\omega_X$-transforms with the normalized bigraded Frobenius characteristics computed by Boixeda Alvarez--Hameister--Ma for the torus-equivariant Borel--Moore homology of the positive parts of homogeneous affine Springer fibers. We introduce cyclic LLT polynomials and determine their monomial expansions, yielding explicit monomial formulas for these elliptic Hall algebra expressions in terms of cyclic parking functions. These results extend the affine Springer fiber identity and monomial formula of Carlsson--Mellit from integral slopes to arbitrary positive rational slopes.

papers.title: On the average eccentricity of Eulerian and bipartite Eulerian digraphs
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be an Eulerian digraph of order $n$ and minimum degree $\delta$. We prove that the average eccentricity of $D$ satisfies $\avec(D) \leq \frac{3n}{\delta+1}$, and that $\avec(D) \leq \frac{2n}{\delta}+2$ if $D$ is bipartite. We show that both bounds are best possible apart from an additive constant and the $\delta+1$ versus $\delta+2$ gap (resp.\ the $\delta$ versus $\delta+1$ gap in the bipartite case), where the average eccentricity of the extremal examples shows that $\avec = \frac{3n}{\delta+2}-2$ in general and $\avec = \frac{2n}{\delta+1}-\frac{5}{2}$ in the bipartite case for $\delta \geq 2$. We further conjecture that these values are the true maxima up to an additive constant (for $\delta \geq 3$ in the bipartite case).

papers.title: Monochromatic or rainbow triangles in the triangular lattice
papers.abstract: Erd\H{o}s, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer, and Straus conjectured that for each non-equilateral triangle $\operatorname{T}$, every 2-coloring of the plane contains a congruent copy of $\operatorname{T}$ with monochromatic vertex set. We confirm this conjecture for triangles with a ratio $\sqrt{7/3}$ between two side lengths. We further prove that every coloring of the plane, regardless of the number of colors used, contains congruent copies of 36 specific triangles with monochromatic or rainbow vertex sets, partially answering a question of Geh\'er, Sagdeev, and T\'oth. Both these results were obtained by considering finite configurations on the triangular lattice.

papers.title: Stabilization of the zero forcing number of generalized Petersen graphs
papers.abstract: We show that the zero forcing number of the generalized Petersen graph $P(n,k)$ is $2k+2$ whenever $n\ge 2k^2+k+1$. We prove this by showing that the zero forcing number of the infinite generalized Petersen graph $P(\infty,k)$ is $2k+2$ and bounding the width of the closure of every set of at most $2k+1$ vertices. This bound gives a threshold on $n$ beyond which the projection of such a closure onto $P(n,k)$ does not wrap around. Combined with an exhaustive computer search for smaller $n$, we determine the zero forcing number of every $P(n,k)$ for $k\le 5$.

papers.title: Properties of the Dichromatic Polynomial
papers.abstract: The chromatic polynomial is a well-studied function of graphs whose coefficients, factorization, and other properties are well-known to encode structural information about the underlying graph. An analogous notion of graph colouring exists for directed graphs which is also well-studied, but little is yet known about the corresponding dichromatic polynomial. We investigate properties of the dichromatic polynomial, including its coefficient interpretations, root-dense regions, and asymptotic growth. We also show that chordal digraphs' polynomials split into linear factors in a way analogous to the undirected case, confirm a conjecture on dichromatic uniqueness posed by Gonz\'alez-Moreno et al., and study the density of dichromatic polynomials within certain larger families of polynomials.

papers.title: On the Chromatic Number of Cayley Tables of Dihedral Groups
papers.abstract: A coloring of a Latin square $L$ is an assignment of $k$ colors to its cells such that no two cells sharing a row, a column, or a symbol receive the same color. The smallest $k$ for which such a coloring exists is called the \emph{chromatic number} of $L$, denoted by $\chi(L)$. The Cayley table of a finite group $G$ of order $n$ is a Latin square, which we denote by $L_G$. It is known that $\chi(L_G)\ne n+1$, so either $\chi(L_G)=n$ or $\chi(L_G)\ge n+2$. Moreover, $\chi(L_G)=n$ if and only if every Sylow $2$-subgroup of $G$ is trivial or non-cyclic, which completely characterizes the finite groups whose Cayley tables attain the lower bound $n$. In this paper, we consider the dihedral group $D_n$ of order $2n$, where $n$ is odd. Since $D_n$ has a cyclic Sylow $2$-subgroup, it follows that $\chi(L_{D_n})\ge 2n+2$. We prove that this bound is sharp, that is, $\chi(L_{D_n})=2n+2$.
